audited_plan.image_description: A museum display of a Triceratops fossil skeleton. The image shows the articulated bones, including the skull with three horns and large frill, rib cage, spine, and limb bones, mounted on a rocky base against a dark background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount clearly displays the characteristic three-horn arrangement: two long brow horns and one shorter nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The checkpoint describes soft tissue (keratinous beak). As this is a fossil skeleton, only the bony rostral bone is visible; the keratinous sheath is missing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeleton is mounted in a quadrupedal stance with thick, pillar-like limb bones consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large bony frill is the most dominant feature of the skull assembly, extending significantly behind the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as a solid bony structure (not a lattice) with visible undulations/bumps along the margin (epoccipitals).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This checkpoint refers to skin texture/integument. A fossil skeleton consists only of bone; no skin or scales are preserved or visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visual comparison of the limb bones confirms the forelimbs are shorter than the hindlimbs, and the spine slopes downward toward the shoulders.
The visible portion of the tail vertebral column is relatively short and robust compared to other dinosaur taxa.
